title: Your First Istanbul Trip: What to Know Before You Arrive
excerpt: Entry requirements, which airport you’re flying into, where to stay, how the Istanbulkart works and a sightseeing plan that leaves room to enjoy it — the practical details to sort before your first Istanbul trip.
bodyHtml:
Your First Istanbul Trip: What to Know Before You Arrive

A few days in Istanbul can include historic sights, long breakfasts, neighborhood walks, and time on the water. The key is to organize the practical details before you arrive, then give yourself enough space to enjoy being there.

For your first visit, start with the essentials: entry requirements, a convenient place to stay, an airport transfer, and a manageable sightseeing plan.

Check your passport and visa requirements. Entry rules for Türkiye depend on your nationality and travel document. Some visitors qualify for visa-free entry, while others need an e-Visa or a visa arranged in advance. Check the passport validity requirements that apply to you through the Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Our guide to visa-free stays, e-Visas and the 90/180 rule explains how your days are counted.

If you need an e-Visa, use the official government website. Keep your travel documents and accommodation confirmations accessible offline, along with your hotel’s full address and contact details.

Know which airport you’re flying into. Istanbul Airport uses the code IST, while Sabiha Gökçen Airport uses SAW. Check your booking carefully before arranging transport—and check your return flight too, as you may depart from a different airport.

From Istanbul Airport, options include the M11 metro, Havaist airport buses, and taxis. Compare the complete journey to your hotel, including connections and walking, rather than looking only at the airport leg: the M11 runs to Gayrettepe, so reaching the Old City means changing to the M2 and often the T1 tram as well. Turkish Airlines’ transport guide explains the main options.

Sabiha Gökçen connects to Kadıköy on the M4 metro, with onward connections elsewhere in the city. Consult the airport’s metro information when planning your route.

Our guide to getting from IST and Sabiha Gökçen into the city compares the options in more detail. Choose transport that suits your arrival time and luggage. Keep your first day flexible, and plan your return transfer before departure day, allowing extra time for traffic or connections.

Choose your hotel around your main interests. On a short trip, a convenient location can save considerable travel time. Put your accommodation and your sightseeing priorities on the same map before booking.

Three areas to consider are:

  • Sultanahmet: A practical starting point if your main interests are the historic sights around Hagia Sophia, the Blue Mosque, and Topkapı Palace.

  • Karaköy or Galata: Worth considering for a mix of sightseeing, cafés, restaurants, and neighborhood walks. Check the approach to your hotel for hills and steps.

  • Kadıköy: An option if you want to spend more time on the Asian side and are happy to allow time for journeys to the Old City. Our Kadıköy guide covers what to do, where to eat and how to get there.

Explore the areas through the official Istanbul destination guide. Recent hotel reviews can help you check practical details such as noise, lift access, and the walk from public transport.

Keep your sightseeing plan realistic. Choose one or two major attractions per day and group nearby places together. This leaves room for queues, meals, and the smaller discoveries that make a trip memorable.

Check opening days, visitor arrangements, and ticket options directly with the attractions you most want to visit. Book ahead where appropriate, but allow time for security checks and entry queues. Avoid scheduling an important timed visit immediately after your flight.

Public transport is useful to understand before you arrive. Istanbulkart is a transport payment card used across services including buses, metros, trams, Marmaray, and public ferries. Cards can be bought and reloaded at designated machines and sales points. The city’s Istanbulkart guide explains the options, and our Istanbulkart guide covers how to get the most from it.

Save your hotel’s nearest useful stop, look up journeys before setting out, and check return services if you plan to stay out late.

Prepare your payment options and phone. Bring a payment card and some Turkish lira for smaller purchases. Check your bank’s overseas charges before traveling, and confirm the amount and currency before approving a payment. Use current prices when budgeting for attractions and activities.

Arrange roaming or mobile data before departure. Download an offline map and save your hotel address in Turkish. Our guide to SIM cards and mobile data covers the local options. A small power bank is helpful when your phone holds your directions, tickets, and reservations.

Pack comfortable walking shoes and clothing suited to the forecast for your travel dates. Layers give you flexibility, particularly if you plan to spend time on the water.

For mosque visits, wear clothing that covers your shoulders and knees; women should cover their hair. Free scarves are usually provided at the entrance, but bringing your own is easier. Remove shoes before entering carpeted prayer areas and follow the guidance at each entrance. Visitor access may pause around prayers. This mosque etiquette guide explains the basics. For more on local customs, see Turkish Basics and Etiquette.

Two more guides worth a look before you go: how to stay safe without becoming paranoid, and the emergency numbers worth saving on your phone.

Planning dates for your trip? Our visiting page puts the city’s guides, events and hosts in one place.

Keep your first evening simple. Check in, take a short walk, and find somewhere nearby for dinner. You’ll have time to get your bearings, settle into the city, and begin your first full day feeling ready to explore.
